check_text:
protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 note).

1. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 12 wells never mixed after enzyme went in (5% of the well)
   line 59:  p20.dispense(1, dest_well)
   At line 59 the robot added enzyme to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in
   slot 2, which already held water, buffer, plasmid 1, plasmid 2 and 10 more (this line did
   it 12 times). The addition was 5% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the
   run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their
   own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is
   vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the
   instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2 after line 59:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [330cec47c9b6]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: 12 wells never mixed after enzyme went in (5% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 59 the robot added enzyme to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2, which already held water, buffer, plasmid 1, plasmid 2 and 10 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 5% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2 after line 59: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
